newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks close strong on peso relief.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks close strong on peso relief.

text.p: Mexican stocks held on to earlier gains to close up for the second day in a row on Friday, as buyers returned in the wake of a more stable peso and interest rates, analysts and traders said.
"Stocks had been hit too hard ... and fundamentals like foreign exchange and interest rate stability clearly help," said Esteban Rojas, deputy reasearch director at the Arka brokerage in Mexico City.
The blue chip IPC index was up 42.49 points, or 1.32 percent, at 3,255.82. At 94.6 million shares traded, volume was brisk, albeit not as spectacular as on Thursday.

"The peso seems to have reacted to support at eight to the dollar, and we're seeing two-way traffic at current rates, which we see as an appropriate year-end level," said Ramon Ruiz, sales trader at the Bankers Trust Latam equities desk in New York.
The benchmark 48-hour peso closed 2.7 centavos firmer 7.9530 per dollar.
Cetes, or Treasury bill, overnight rates meanwhile closed down 1.25 percentage points at 30.0 percent.
On the broad market, a total of 108 stocks were traded, of which gainers outnumbered losers by 71 to 21.
Bus and truck makers Dina headed the leaders, up 1.04 pesos (13 cents ) to 5.06 pesos (64 cents), following the announcement of a debt exchange offer by the firm and MCII Holdings.

Mining and autoparts firm Sanluis was also a prominent gainer, up 2.30 pesos (29 cents) to 42.60 ($5.36). Traders noted a Wall Street Journal article about favourable prospects for the Mexican autoparts industry, and that Credit Lyonnais had initiated coverage of Sanluis with buy recommendation.
Several Mexican ADRs ended up, despite a 0.12 percent fall in the Dow Jones. Telmex, for example, gained 1/8 to 30-5/8, and its L series was up six centavos (1 cent) to 12.20 pesos ($1.53).
Food company Gruma headed the losers, down 60 centavos (8 cents) to 39.30 pesos ($4.93). Gruma had announced a global stock offer on Thursday.
